status_summary: No new executive order stating a general no-degree rule was found. Executive Order 14170, signed 2025-01-20, directs a Federal Hiring Plan with technical and alternative assessments and does not mention degree requirements, and the Merit Hiring Plan memorandum of 2025-05-29 states that agencies shall revamp position descriptions and eliminate requirements that are not relevant, such as degree requirements, citing Executive Order 13932 of 2020. On 2026-04-13 the OPM Director issued a memorandum adopting a competency-based qualification standard for the Information Technology Management Series, 2210, whose standard on opm.gov states that education may not be required for, or substituted for, demonstrating the required competencies, which is an occupation-level step of the kind the Mandate describes. A trade publication in April 2026 reported that OPM was reviewing more than 600 job classifications for possible removal of degree requirements, with agencies still rewriting qualification standards.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14170, Reforming the Federal Hiring Process and Restoring Merit to Government Service, was signed (published 2025-01-30, document 2025-02094); section 2(b)(iii) calls for technical and alternative assessments, and the order does not address degree requirements.

The Merit Hiring Plan memorandum was issued by the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy and the Acting Director of OPM; section II.A states that agencies shall revamp position descriptions and eliminate requirements that are not relevant, such as degree requirements, with no deadline.

The OPM Director (Scott Kupor) issued a memorandum on competency-based qualification standards for the Information Technology Management Series, 2210. The standard on opm.gov states that education may not be required for, or used in place of, demonstrating the specified competencies and that the former entry-level education distinction is no longer a minimum qualification, while agencies may require specific credentials where the job needs them. The memorandum itself does not mention degrees or state an effective date.

title: Executive order: no college degree required for federal jobs unless the job demands it
uncertainties: Searches run: two by the researcher (opm.gov, federalregister.gov and trade-press terms on degree requirements, Executive Order 13932 and the Merit Hiring Plan); the reviewer ran none and re-read the memorandum, the order and the trade article. Executive Order 13932 (signed 2020-06-26) limited minimum education requirements to cases where legally required, per the CRS Insight; the 2025 memorandum cites it as a standing direction, and no revocation was found, but its status was not confirmed on the Federal Register. The 600-classification figure comes from a trade publication that does not cite an OPM document for it. The memorandum's degree language sits inside a broader skills-based hiring directive with no deadline. c03-05 covers skills-based assessments; this record is the degree-requirement element only. In the 2026-10-17 review the memorandum was re-read in full on opm.gov: its signatories are the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy and the Acting OPM Director, section II.A uses mandatory language for agencies to drop irrelevant requirements such as degree requirements, the first section lists eliminating unnecessary degree requirements as a key element, and no deadline is set. EO 14170 appears at 90 FR 8621, and its section 2(a) set a 120-day deadline for the Federal Hiring Plan (per the researcher's reading of the Federal Register). On 2026-11-10 the OPM memorandum of 2026-04-13 for the 2210 series and OPM's standard page were read on opm.gov; the memorandum is silent on degrees and the education statement comes from the standard page, which carries no date or effective date. A Nextgov report of 2026-04-15 describes the change as covering government technology jobs. A web search for a governmentwide order or rule on degree requirements after 2026-04-13 found none; the stage and progress are unchanged.
